sections.history: Nachiyarkoil, also called Thirunaraiyur, lies a few kilometres south-east of Kumbakonam. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams in Chola Nadu, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, who calls the shrine Mani Mada Koil, the temple of the jewelled mansions, and the Lord "Naraiyur Nindra Nambi". The temple is attributed to Kochengat Chola, and is noted as the only Vishnu temple credited to him, his other foundations being Shiva temples. Tradition adds that Thirumangai Alvar received the Vaishnava initiation, the Pancha Samskaram, from the Lord here. The Goddess is regarded as the principal deity, which is why the village is called Nachiyar Koil, the temple of the Nachiyar.
sections.architecture: The sanctum stands under the Srinivasa Vimanam, and the temple tank is the Manimukta Pushkarini. Thirunaraiyur Nambi is worshipped as Srinivasa Perumal, with the Goddess Vanjulavalli Nachiyar in her own prominent shrine. The most distinctive feature is the Kal Garuda, the stone Garuda in his own shrine, whose image is carved of stone yet is carried in procession. The temple is built in the Dravidian manner of the Chola country.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of the sage Medhavi, a devotee of Vishnu, who wished to have the Lord as his son-in-law. Lakshmi appeared as his daughter Vanjulavalli, and Vishnu came to Thirunaraiyur and wedded her; the Goddess is therefore honoured here before the Lord. The Kal Garuda carries its own tradition: when taken out in procession, the stone image is said to grow heavier, so that four bearers lift it at the shrine and many more by the time it leaves the temple. It is believed to relieve the afflictions of the planets.
sections.festivals: The Kal Garuda procession is the temple's best-known observance, held twice a year, on the fourth day of the Margazhi festival and of the Panguni festival. Vaikunta Ekadashi is also observed. Confirm festival dates locally, as they follow the Tamil almanac; Kal Garuda days are very crowded.
sections.experience: Come to see the Goddess honoured before the Lord, and the Kal Garuda in his shrine. A pilgrim who reads Thirumangai Alvar's Mani Mada Koil verses will find the name still living in the village. The temple is quieter outside festival days and combines well with other Divya Desams near Kumbakonam.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Vaikunta Ekadashi is the busiest day. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Nachiyarkoil lies roughly 8–10 km south-east of Kumbakonam, in the Cauvery delta. Kumbakonam is the nearest railway station, and Tiruchirappalli International Airport the nearest major airport; buses and taxis from Kumbakonam cover the road journey.
